notes.name: Wikipedia · Jean-Michel Basquiat
notes.q: He had his first American one-man show at the Annina Nosei Gallery in March 1982.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Jean-Michel Basquiat
notes.q: By the summer of 1982, Basquiat had left the Annina Nosei Gallery, and gallerist Bruno Bischofberger became his worldwide art dealer.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Jean-Michel Basquiat
notes.q: In June 1982, at 21, Basquiat became the youngest artist to ever take part in Documenta in Kassel, Germany.

src.name: Wikipedia · Jean-Michel Basquiat
src.q: He also painted in Modena for his second Italian exhibition in March 1982.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Jean-Michel Basquiat
notes.q: In February 1986, Basquiat traveled to Atlanta, Georgia, for an exhibition of his drawings at Fay Gold Gallery.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Jean-Michel Basquiat
notes.q: In October 1986, Basquiat flew to Ivory Coast for an exhibition of his work organized by Bruno Bischofberger at the French Cultural Institute in Abidjan.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Jean-Michel Basquiat
notes.q: In November 1986, at 25 years old, Basquiat became the youngest artist given an exhibition at Kestner-Gesellschaft in Hanover, Germany.

src.name: Wikipedia · Jean-Michel Basquiat
src.q: For what would be his last exhibition on the West Coast, Basquiat returned to Los Angeles for his show at the Gagosian Gallery in January 1986.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Jean-Michel Basquiat
notes.q: Following his exhibition at the Vrej Baghoomian Gallery in New York in April 1988, Basquiat traveled to Maui in June to withdraw from drug use.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Jean-Michel Basquiat
notes.q: In January 1988, Basquiat traveled to Paris for his exhibition at the Yvon Lambert Gallery and to Düsseldorf for an exhibition at the Hans Mayer Gallery.
